justifications.functional_suitability: The architecture addresses all functional requirements: Scoring Engine Container evaluates transactions via Inference Engine Component (R-01), Case Management Container provides analyst review workflows (R-02), and the Sidecar Model Deployment Pipeline supports atomic hot-reloading of models and rules without downtime (R-03).
justifications.performance_efficiency: The Go/Rust Scoring Engine Container, in-memory Go channels, ElastiCache Redis caching for feature velocity, and asynchronous logging via Audit Dispatcher Component with a ring-buffer pattern directly support the sub-50ms P99 latency target under 3,000 TPS.
justifications.compatibility: Payment Gateway / Acquirer connects cleanly via standard REST/gRPC over TLS 1.3, while Identity Provider integrates using OAuth2/OIDC. However, payment domain interchange standards (e.g., ISO 8583 or ISO 20022 formats) are not explicitly addressed.
justifications.usability: Fraud Analyst & Risk Manager is provided with a dedicated data-masked UI within the Case Management Container, authenticated via IdP. However, operational usability tooling for the three-engineer team to monitor deployments and system health is not explicitly represented.
justifications.reliability: API Gateway lists circuit breaking and Alerting & Dead-Letter Monitor handles backpressure, but the explicit fail-open or fallback mechanism required to ensure payment processing is not blocked for over 1 minute during scoring outages (R-07) is missing.
justifications.security: PCI-DSS constraints and R-05/R-06 are tackled via data-masked UI, IdP RBAC, and Compliance Vault S3 Writer with S3 Object Lock. However, the dedicated tokenization mechanism or PCI vault container for handling raw PANs is omitted.
justifications.maintainability: Clear separation of concerns between stateless Scoring Engine Container, Case Management Container, and managed AWS data services matches the three-engineer team constraint well. However, multiple implementation languages (Go, Rust, Node.js, Python) increase cognitive overhead.
justifications.portability: The system targets AWS eu-west-1 as specified, but deep architectural coupling to proprietary services like DynamoDB, EventBridge, CloudTrail, and S3 Object Lock makes migration to alternative clouds or on-premises environments difficult without significant redesign.

PERF-01.justification: Compiled Go/Rust services, local ONNX runtime inference, and Redis caching avoid hot-path database queries. Asynchronous audit dispatch ensures the evaluation loop stays well below 50 ms P99 under 3,000 TPS.
sensitivity_points: Network latency between Scoring Engine and ElastiCache Redis cluster.
Model evaluation execution time within ONNX runtime.
tradeoffs: Using in-memory feature caching improves latency but risks stale velocity counters.

PERF-02.justification: Scoring engine and case management are isolated in separate ECS containers. Real-time scoring relies on ElastiCache and in-memory models rather than primary case tables, preventing analyst UI queries from degrading scoring P99 latency.
sensitivity_points: DynamoDB read/write capacity allocation between real-time scoring and case queries.
tradeoffs: Single-table DynamoDB design saves operational cost but risks cross-workload capacity contention.

AVAIL-01.justification: While API Gateway specifies circuit breaking in its container summary, Level 3 shows only AWS WAF and HTTP API Router with no concrete fallback engine or audited stand-in decision mechanism when scoring fails.
sensitivity_points: Absence of fallback execution engine or Lambda when ECS scoring containers fail.
Circuit breaker fallback routing policy at API Gateway.
tradeoffs: Fail-open payment approvals preserve availability but increase direct fraud financial risk.

AVAIL-02.justification: The Audit Dispatcher decouples the critical scoring path via a local in-memory ring buffer and asynchronous queueing to SQS/DynamoDB, protecting P99 latency while preserving audit logs during downstream slowness.
sensitivity_points: Ring-buffer size limits during extended downstream database degradation.
Backpressure handling when flushing audit logs to DynamoDB or SQS.
tradeoffs: Asynchronous ring buffering protects scoring latency but risks memory exhaustion during sustained outages.

MOD-01.justification: The S3-backed sidecar deployment pipeline dynamically mounts updated models to local shared volumes for atomic hot-reloading without service restarts, recording the active model version in the decision payload for auditability.
sensitivity_points: File system atomic pointer swap speed on shared ECS task volumes.
Model payload validation prior to switching active ONNX inference instances.
tradeoffs: Hot-reloading models locally enables zero downtime but causes temporary per-node version discrepancies.

MOD-02.justification: Analysts update rules via Case Management into DynamoDB and ElastiCache. The Scoring Engine dynamically loads updated rules from cache, emitting rule execution traces into the audit dispatcher with zero deployment downtime.
sensitivity_points: Cache invalidation and propagation latency across Redis and Scoring Engine replicas.
Rule expression syntax validation before publishing to shared stores.
tradeoffs: Dynamic rule polling avoids deployment downtime but requires distributed cache consistency checks.

SEC-01.justification: Data-masked UI and tokenization prevent compromised analyst accounts from obtaining plain-text PANs. However, the architecture relies on generic CloudTrail and dead-letter monitoring rather than an explicit anomaly detection system for 15-minute access alerts.
sensitivity_points: Card PAN tokenization enforcement before storage in the transactional database.
Absence of dedicated behavioral anomaly detection or SIEM integration.
tradeoffs: Strict field masking prevents credential exposure but restricts analysts investigating complex fraud patterns.

SEC-02.justification: Decisions include inputs, model versions, and explanations, streamed via audit loggers into AWS S3 with Object Lock (WORM). This guarantees tamper-evident 7-year retention and predictable indexing for retrieval well within one working day.
sensitivity_points: S3 Object Lock retention policy enforcement in compliance mode.
Preservation of inputs, model version, and explanation metadata in archived records.
tradeoffs: Immutable WORM storage guarantees audit compliance but incurs cumulative 7-year storage expenses.
